We are recruiting a PhD student (fully funded 3-year position) on Human-Computer Interaction and Extended Reality to join the Human-Centred Computing Section at the University of Copenhagen.

Application deadline 1 February 2026 Earliest start date: 1 June 2026

The PhD project:
Extended reality (XR) technologies, such as virtual reality and augmented reality enable experiences that are impossible or difficult in the real world. Prior work has suggested that such experiences in XR can influence users' behaviour outside of XR, for example, by adopting characteristics of an avatar one embodied in XR. This PhD project will work towards identifying, investigating, and evaluating the underlying mechanisms of XR as a behaviour change technology. Specifically, it will explore how XR qualities (e.g., embodiment and presence) affect behaviour and how XR can be leveraged to encourage positive change. Within this topic, the PhD student will have much freedom to shape the focus of their work and the research questions they are interested in. The specific research direction will be developed together with the PhD student. Possible directions include (but are not limited to): studying how XR qualities influence perspective-taking in VR/AR, exploring stated-preference methods for XR-based behaviour change, personalizing behaviour change interventions using generative AI, systematically investigating benefits of XR on improving behaviour change techniques.

The research environment:
The project’s funding comes from the Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence, a 5-university Danish research endeavor, and the Human-Centered Computing research section at the University of Copenhagen’s Department of Computer Science. Both the centre and research section are highly international and well-funded, working on a broad range of fundamental research topics.
